newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corn supplies tight for a year -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corn supplies tight for a year -- USDA.

text.p: U.S. corn supplies will remain relatively tight in the next year, and prices -- while dropping from recent records -- are expected to stay strong, USDA said in its Agricultural Outlook summary Thursday.
The 1996/97 season-average farm price is projected at $3-$3.40 per bushel, nearly unchanged from 1995/96, it said.

Continued large domestic demand will increase total corn use slightly in 1996/97. But the impact of other grain sectors will be important, especially for feed use. Higher production of other grains suggests a slight easing of pressure on corn, the summary said.
A drop in U.S. corn exports is anticipated this year as competitors' exportable supplies of corn and other feed grains increase and as world import demand for corn slacks off slightly, USDA said.
